name: maybe_Field_ActorAction_UpdateMoveDirection

summary: Computes the field actor's movement direction for this frame: reads the stick vector (or the look stick), normalises it, rotates it by the actor's rotation quaternion, rejects a direction nearly perpendicular to the actor's wall normal, and sets the work movement-mode byte and speed accordingly.

name: maybe_Ui_MapWindow_RefreshEntry

summary: Refreshes the condition rows 0x3A/0x3B/0x3C (plus 0xB5/0x100) of a battle monster: for each row it checks the member's two equipped items against the condition record types 0x0B/0x10/0x12 and re-rolls the row value when one matches.
evidence: The equipped-slot lookups (func_006292F0) and condition-record type bytes are now readable and consistent with a status-row refresh; the f_C type ids 0x0B/0x10/0x12 are still unexplained, so 'condition flags' stays a description rather than a proven field name.

name: maybe_Text_Row_ApplySpacingPresetB
summary: Picks the first row id present on the object from a second preset group (0x27/0x28/0xA4/0xAD/0xB0/0x29/0x2A/0x108/0x103/0x11E/0x120), takes that row's value and marks the layout dirty if the scaled value is non-zero.
evidence: The same fallback ladder as the A preset at 0x00497FD4 but with a different id group, and the trailing Text_MarkLayoutDirty/0.01 test confirms it only triggers a layout rebuild; what the looked-up value means is still unclear.

name: maybe_Battle_ApplyMonsterEffect
signature: void maybe_Battle_ApplyMonsterEffect(u32 effectId, BattleWork* work, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, int arg5, int arg6, int arg7, int arg8, int arg9, u32 arg10)
summary: Loads the display rows for a monster's effect/condition: with a concrete effect id it formats the effect text and loads the condition record for the record's 4/8/other type; with 0xFF it instead takes the member's equipped item, switches on its category and refreshes the matching condition rows.
evidence: Named callees maybe_Monster_FormatEffectText, maybe_Battle_Monster_LoadConditionRecord and Text_MarkLayoutDirty show a display-refresh path rather than damage application; the category bytes come from the item record (+0x29), so 'ApplyMonsterEffect' overstates what happens.

name: maybe_Monster_FormatEffectText
signature: void maybe_Monster_FormatEffectText(u32 effectId, int arg2, int arg3, MonsterWork* work, u32 arg5, u8 arg6, u8 arg7)
summary: Builds the effect/ailment text rows for a battle unit: copies the default layout table, fills the parameter block from the effect record and the caster's monster record (display bytes at +10/+0xB) and appends the eight rows through 0x00326428.
evidence: The body is a row builder (maybe_Ui_CopyDefaultLayoutTable + an 8-iteration 0x00326428 loop) rather than a string formatter, and its callers (0x488C24, 0x49100C, 0x491BC8, 0x497690) are all battle text-row builders; the exact row content is still opaque.

name: Battle_Monster_GetStateIcon
signature: u32 Battle_Monster_GetStateIcon(u32 monsterId, BattleWork* work, int arg3, u32 ctx)
summary: Returns the status icon index (0..6, 0xFF = none) for a battle monster: the record's own state byte f_295 wins, otherwise the f_2E8 bits and the battle work's action rows 0x62/99/100/0x65/0x66/0x67 pick the display state, with the equipped item's state as the fallback.
evidence: The record-based branch (f_295, f_2E8 bits 0/1) and the work-row ladder are both explicit, and the fallback goes through the now-named Item_LookupRecord plus 0x66C5F4 on the equipped item, i.e. a state/icon selector by construction.

name: Text_GetRowRecordCopy
summary: Returns a mutable copy of a text-row template: copies the 0x63FD24 record's ten header words, its 0x1E-byte block, four more fields at +0x46..+0x52 and the two trailing string fields into the caller's buffer (the apparent stack locals are the structure-return buffer).
evidence: The function writes a complete 0x1B0-byte record and stores nothing else, which is the classic hidden-return-pointer shape; its only caller Text_CalcRowRect (0x00488C24) reads that copy afterwards, so 'get a copy of the row record' is now supported.

name: maybe_Battle_Action_GetRowValue
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_Action_GetRowValue(u16 actionId, BattleUnit* unit, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, u32 arg5)
summary: Returns the numeric value shown on an action row: special units (+0x10 set) use the effect-value helper, otherwise the value is one of the record's four words at +0x13C/+0x13E/+0x140/+0x142, selected by the flags at +0x189/+0x187/+0x185/+0x184.
evidence: The id is resolved by 0x0063FD24, which the project established as the action-record table, and the caller Text_CalcRowRect builds a battle text row from it; the 'monster' wording was only the first pass's guess.

name: maybe_Battle_Monster_UpdateConditionRow
signature: void maybe_Battle_Monster_UpdateConditionRow(int effectId, int member, int targetUnit, int slotOrFlag, u32 arg5)
summary: Refreshes one condition row for a battle unit: resolves the member and its equipped slot, reads the target's monster-record display byte, rebuilds the row through maybe_Monster_FormatEffectText when a real effect id is supplied, and marks the text layout dirty.
evidence: The named callees (func_0035EB98 member lookup, func_006292F0 equipped slot, func_0063DCA4 monster record, maybe_Monster_FormatEffectText, Text_MarkLayoutDirty) match a per-row refresh, but 'condition' still rests on the effect-id argument rather than a decoded field.

name: Battle_Actor_GetStateIcon
summary: Party-actor twin of Battle_Monster_GetStateIcon: returns f_DD when set, otherwise uses the f_FF flag bits with the battle work's action rows 0x62/99/100/0x65/0x66/0x67 to pick icon 0..6, falling back to the equipped item's state.
evidence: The body is the same ladder as the monster variant with party-record offsets (f_DD/f_FF), and the item fallback again uses the named Item_LookupRecord; the caller context (battle message row building) is unchanged.

name: Battle_Monster_CalcBarSpan
signature: u64 Battle_Monster_CalcBarSpan(BattleUnit* self, int barIndex, int scaled)
summary: Computes the filled width of one of the unit's two gauge bars (HP for barIndex 0, MP for 1): adds the record's bar origin, the current/reference span and the bar's offset, optionally scaling by the global ratio, and returns the end value packed with the flag.
evidence: The two branches are identical except for the record offsets (+0xEB8/+0xEC8 vs +0xEBA/+0xECA), which is exactly the HP/MP pair used by the surrounding row builders; the old 'HpBarSpan' name only described half of it.

name: Battle_UnitModelA_Update
signature: void Battle_UnitModelA_Update(UnitModel* self, int arg2, int frameArg)
summary: Per-frame update of the 0x1A5 unit-model variant: ticks the anim channels, motion state and elapsed counter, runs the shared part/SE updates, then switches to the paired (vtable+0xA8) or solo (+0xA4) display variant depending on whether a live model-0x1A5 unit is present.
evidence: Every step is a named engine call (Anim_UpdateChannels, Model_UpdateMotionState, Battle_UnitModel_UpdateParts, Battle_UnitModel_PlayAnimSe), but 0x0042A438 is already named Battle_UnitModel_Update for the plain base update; this one adds the 0x1A5 paired/solo switch, hence the A suffix.

name: Battle_UnitModelB_Update
signature: void Battle_UnitModelB_Update(UnitModelB* self, int arg2, int frameArg)
summary: Second unit-model update variant: same channel/motion/part update as 0x004A7F08 but keyed on model id 0x18F when deciding between the paired and solo display variants.
evidence: Byte-identical to 0x004A7F08 except the searched model id (0x18F), and the same named update/anim helpers are called; the B tag keeps the two template copies distinguishable.

name: Battle_Model_UpdateVisibility
signature: void Battle_Model_UpdateVisibility(BattleModel* self, int frameArg, int arg3)
summary: Per-frame update of a battle model with visibility handling: hides the model while its cutscene actor is model 0x350, scans the four event actor lists for the 0x18F/0x1A5 models, runs the shared model update and then sets the material/visibility byte +0x26 to 0 or 0xFF.
evidence: The vtable+0x44 hide call with model id 0x350, the four-list scan for the same ids as 0x004A7F08/0x004A8688 and the explicit f_26 = 0 / 0xFF stores make the visibility role concrete rather than inferred.

name: maybe_PartyStatus_LoadNewestRecord
signature: void maybe_PartyStatus_LoadNewestRecord(u32 arg1, int rebuildPanel, int arg3)
summary: Builds the party status view from the stored time-tagged records: fills the cached party sizes, picks the newest record by comparing Svc_Time timestamps across the record table, copies the winning 0x44-byte party slot and rebuilds the status panel.
evidence: The body is dominated by Svc_Time_IsValidDateTimeRecord / Svc_Time_MakeTimestampFromRecord record selection and ends in maybe_Party_ShiftSkillSlots plus maybe_Ui_PartyStatusPanel_Build; there is no slot-machine code at all, so the 'Casino_Slot_InitState' label was simply wrong.

name: Field_SceneNode_OnCommand
signature: void Field_SceneNode_OnCommand(Field_SceneNode* self, int command, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Command virtual of a field scene node: command 6 plays one of two named animations chosen by the f_297 variant, and command 0 releases the node's animation instances, makes every field actor play animation 6 and plays SE 0x103 (the 'everyone reacts' gimmicks).
evidence: The command constants, the Field_SceneNode_CheckActiveFlag variant test and the named Field_Gadget/Sound_PlaySeById calls line up with a virtual command handler; the two animation names come from the 0x7C22DF/0x7C22E2 literal pool.

name: Field_SceneNode_TriggerCommand22
signature: u32 Field_SceneNode_TriggerCommand22(Field_SceneNode* self, int arg2, int arg3, int arg4)
summary: Sends gadget command 0x22 with the node's own argument when the f_297 variant is 0, and returns 0 without doing anything otherwise.
evidence: The body is a single guarded Field_Gadget_AddAndTriggerCommand(work->f_6C, 0x22, self[1]) call; there is nothing else for it to be.

name: maybe_Ui_MessagePanel_HideOrShowByFlag
summary: Shows or hides a message-panel pane depending on the mode byte at self+4: mode 0 runs the pane's show slots (+0x54/+0x3C) with command 4, any other mode runs the hide slots (+0x58/+0x40) and plays SE 0x102.
evidence: The two vtable pairs with constant 4 and the SE 0x102/0x103 split mirror the sibling 0x004DD340, but the byte test goes through Field_SceneNode_CheckActiveFlag, which is a reused generic flag helper, so the 'mode' meaning is still an interpretation.

name: Field_Gimmick3107_PlayDefaultAction
summary: Resets the gimmick's model and plays its default animation: the f_297 variant selects the animation name ('01' or 'Nut') passed to Anim_PlayByIdForActor, then the animator is pushed to its last frame.
evidence: Named callees maybe_Actor_ApplyModelRecordFast, Anim_PlayByIdForActor and maybe_Field_SceneObject_SetAnimatorLastFrame plus the two literal animation names make the 'play default action' reading concrete.

name: maybe_Ui_MessagePanel_OnModeChange
summary: Tells the target pane to hide and reset (vtable +0x58 and +0x40 with command 4) when the panel's mode byte at +4 is non-zero.
evidence: The two virtual calls with constant 4 match the hide branch of the sibling 0x004DD390, but the mode byte is only read through a generic flag helper and no caller names what triggers the change.

name: Ui_PagedListWindow_CtorVariant
summary: Constructor of the second paged-list window class: constructs the base object, builds the +0x54 sub-object, installs vtables 0x77800C/0x75EB0C, stores the owner and default-constructs the 16-element row array.
evidence: The vtable constants, the owner store at +0x70 and std_ConstructArray(16 elements) are explicit, and the shape matches its near-twin 0x4C5088; both are called from the same inlined screen constructors.

name: maybe_Field_SceneInit_Shared
summary: Creates and initialises one field actor object from the scene record: allocates the 0x330-byte sprite object, registers it in the actor list, builds the 0x84-byte sprite descriptor from the scene record and calls Field_Object2D_InitSpriteActor.
evidence: The named callees (Field_SceneInit_AllocateAlignedBlocks, maybe_Ui_List_BuildRowRecord, Field_Object2D_InitSpriteActor) show it is a single-object creation path, not a whole-scene setup; its only caller is 0x004D7EA4 and no string identifies the scene.

name: Ui_IconCache_Open
signature: int Ui_IconCache_Open(UiIconCache* self, u32 recordId, int expectedCount)
summary: Opens the icon cache for one content record: starts the worker service, looks the record up, rejects a count mismatch, reads both entry-header tables and the entry table, stores the current timestamp and returns 0 (or the lookup error/0xC8810BEA on mismatch).
evidence: Every failure path now goes through named helpers (maybe_Ui_IconCache_Close, maybe_Ui_IconCache_ReleaseService, maybe_Ui_IconCache_ReadEntryHeaders/Table), and the two named callers are the icon-texture loaders; the error-return contract makes the 'open' role explicit.

name: Ui_IconCache_SetPage
summary: Selects and re-reads one of the icon cache's two pages: sends command 0x0D for page 1 or 0x0C for page 0, reads the page header, requests the page block (+0xF3/0x87) and, for page 1, refreshes the entry table.
evidence: The two branches differ only in the command byte and the page pointers, and the trailing calls are the now-named maybe_Ui_IconCache_RequestPage / maybe_Ui_IconCache_ReadEntryTable, matching a page switch.

name: Ui_IconCache_WriteEntry
signature: int Ui_IconCache_WriteEntry(UiIconCache* self, void* out, int arg3, int arg4, int arg5, int arg6)
summary: Serialises one icon-cache entry: prepares/validates it with 0x50A520 and, when that succeeds, writes the raw block through maybe_Ui_IconCache_WriteRawBlock.
evidence: The guard on the prepare result and the single named writer call at the tail leave no other plausible role, and the caller is in the icon-cache consumer range.

name: Ui_IconCache_ResetEntry
summary: Clears the twelve icon-cache state fields at +0x130..+0x160 and resets the shared block header, leaving the object itself intact.
evidence: Twelve explicit field clears followed by the now-named maybe_Ui_IconCache_ResetHeader; there is no allocation or I/O, so this is a state reset.

name: maybe_Container_HashMap_GetCapacity
summary: One-line accessor that returns the second word (+4) of the global container obtained from 0x00658548, or 0 when that global is null; +4 is most likely the capacity/count field.
evidence: Nothing new: 0x00658548 still has no readable C and the only caller is the icon-cache consumer, so which field +4 holds (capacity vs count) cannot be decided from the body.

name: Sound_WaveCache_LoadRaw
signature: u32 Sound_WaveCache_LoadRaw(SoundWaveCache* cache, u32 waveId, SoundAllocator* alloc, u32 size, int publish)
summary: Loads an uncompressed wave into a fresh allocation: looks up the entry, asks the allocator for its size, optionally checks the buffer against the heap range, reads the raw blocks (no decode) and publishes the buffer through the cache's vtable slot +8.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0054B004 confirms the whole path: vtable+0x10 cache lookup, 0x65E398 entry-size lookup (size in r4), allocator vtable+8, optional heap-range check through 0x1180F0/0x1180E0, 0x54B12C read with r3=size, then the cache vtable+8 publish. All seven callers are the wave-cache family.

name: Sound_Player_StartSlotTrackA
signature: int Sound_Player_StartSlotTrackA(SoundPlayer* player, int slot, u32 trackId, u32 arg4)
summary: Stops the slot if it is already running, clears its per-slot alarm (0x6EF854) and hands the (slot, trackId) pair to the A-list track registrar: the readable body inlines the registrar 0x519BF4, which tail-calls 0x517650 with the global list 0x7EF3C4.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0054F48C..0x0054F4E8 shows stop-slot (0x54F6D0), 0x6EF854(slot+0x14,0), 0x51871C(slot), then `pop {r4,r5,r6,lr}; b 0x519BF4` with r0=slot,r1=trackId; 0x519BF4 loads 0x7EF3C4 and branches to 0x517650. The readable body is the inlined registrar, which is why the unaff_ registers appear.

name: Sound_Player_StartSlotTrackB
signature: int Sound_Player_StartSlotTrackB(SoundPlayer* player, int slot, u32 trackId, u32 arg4)
summary: B-variant of the slot restart: stops the running slot, clears the alarm and hands (slot, trackId) to the B-list registrar 0x519C08, which tail-calls 0x5176F4 with the global list 0x7EF3C4.
evidence: Disassembly 0x0054F4F0..0x0054F54C is identical to the A variant up to `b 0x519C08` with r0=slot,r1=trackId, and 0x519C08 loads 0x7EF3C4 and branches to 0x5176F4; the unaff_ registers come from the inlined registrar.

name: Sound_Player_SetSlotTimer
signature: void Sound_Player_SetSlotTimer(SoundPlayer* player, int slot, int ticks)
summary: Arms or cancels the per-slot timer: ticks 0 stops the slot and clears the alarm at slot+0x14, otherwise the alarm is set to ticks/5 so the slot refires later.
evidence: Named Sound_Player_StopSlot plus the explicit /5 magic division and the 0x10-stride slot block make the timer arithmetic readable; the alarm setter itself (0x006EF854) is still unnamed.

name: Sound_Player_StartSlotTrack
signature: int Sound_Player_StartSlotTrack(SoundPlayer* player, int slot, u32 trackId, u32 arg4)
summary: Binds a track to a free player slot: stops the previous track and clears its alarm, applies the three channel parameters (ramp, fade, masked param) and, on success, stores the track handle at +0x290 and the busy flag at +0x294.
evidence: The free-slot guard (+0x294), the named Sound_Player_StopSlot call and the three maybe_Sound_Channel_* helpers that must all succeed make this the straightforward 'start a track in a slot' path.

name: Sound_Player_SetSlotCallback
signature: int Sound_Player_SetSlotCallback(SoundPlayer* player, int slot, u32 callback)
summary: Installs the completion callback for one player slot: stops the slot, clears its alarm, installs the default handler 0x0054F7C0 when none is registered and inserts the caller's callback into the slot's 0xC-stride wait list.
evidence: The default handler constant, the named Sound_Player_StopSlot call and the list insert through 0x0011FCF8 make the 'set the slot callback' reading concrete.

name: Sound_Player_StopAllSlots
summary: Tears down both playback slots: stops each one, hands its two track handles back, zeroes the two 4-byte handle arrays at +0x6C/+0x274 and finally clears the object's open byte.
evidence: The two-slot loop, the named Sound_Player_StopSlot call and the only caller (the sound driver teardown 0x00542580) make this the shutdown path for the player's slots.

name: Sound_Player_TickSlots
summary: Per-frame tick of the two playback slots: advances the volume/envelope ramps and their duration counters, pushes the interpolated volume, reaps finished track handles in state 2 and, when a slot ran, signals the consumer queue through 0x00550B78/0x00550D48.
evidence: The fixed two-slot loop with 0x10-byte stride, the 1.0/0.0 clamp and the handle-state test plus the named Sound_Player_StopSlot path all match a slot tick; 0x00550B78/0x00550D48 are still unnamed but are used by the command executor too.

name: Script_InvokeCallbackPair
signature: void Script_InvokeCallbackPair(unsigned int* out, void* callable, unsigned int arg3)
summary: Calls a Squirrel callable with one extra argument: pushes the callable's stored references plus arg3, invokes it, requires a boolean result, then duplicates the result and the first parameter into two managed reference pairs at out[1..4].
evidence: The now-named Sq_* callees (Sq_VmGetStackSlot, Sq_VmReadStackSlot, Sq_PushRefValue, Sq_VmPop) plus the 0x8000100/0x8000200 boolean type check make the VM call shape explicit; only the caller 0x00579B64 knows what the two refs are used for.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_HidePartsAndNotify
summary: Walks the gimmick's part list, hides each part object through its vtable+0xA4 and spawns the matching effect, and once all parts are handled raises the field's render part count to at least 2, updates both UI panels and plays SE 0xE46.
evidence: Named Field_Gimmick_FindSlotObjectById/Sound_PlaySeById and the per-part effect spawn make the iteration clear, but the vtable slot +0xA4(6,4) and the UI panel slots +0x44/+0x20 are not decoded, so 'hide' remains an interpretation.

name: Field_Gimmick_ApplyPartActionsAndNotify
summary: Applies the stored actions of every gimmick part: resolves the part object by handle, plays its part animation/sound, posts the menu/effect notification, plays the impact SE for parts in state 4/5 and finally rolls the accumulated value and updates the gimmick's command state.
evidence: Named callees Field_Gimmick_FindSlotObjectById, maybe_Menu_NotifyDialogResult and Sound_PlaySeById plus the explicit per-part state test (4/5) make the part-action loop readable; the unnamed 0x5D85AC/0x5D7E28 helpers are the only unexplained step.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_InitSlotEffects
summary: Resets and fills the gimmick's eight 0x14-byte slot records: clears the counters, writes the empty handle sentinel, binds each slot to a part object from the group and assigns randomised start/end ticks, then copies the per-part bars into the two model objects.
evidence: Named Field_Gimmick_FindSlotObjectById plus the explicit 8-slot/0x14-stride clear and the RNG-derived timing fields make the initialisation clear, but 'effects' is only inferred from the later slot consumers.

name: maybe_Actor_GetLookupState
signature: u32 maybe_Actor_GetLookupState(u16 id, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 ctx)
summary: Looks the id up with 0x0063E01C and tests its state byte +0x10 against the values 1/2/3. The decompiled body lost every return value (bare `return;`), so the mapping from state to result is unknown.
evidence: The lookup and the 1/2/3 tests are visible, but all three exits are plain `return;` with no value, i.e. damaged decompilation; the surrounding bind-native neighbours cannot restore the dropped returns.

name: BattleScene_SyncUnitRenderResources
summary: Builds/refreshes the render resources of all battle unit slots: caches the enemy-model handle per slot (12 slots at +0x504, stride 8), loads the battle-2D models, registers the extra resource entries (399/0x1A5/400/0x18E) and finally loads the background model set for the 400 case.
evidence: The whole path is now named (Battle2D_LoadEnemyModel, Pack_HandlePair_MoveAssign, maybe_Ui_AddResourceEntry/AddNamedEntry) and the sole caller is BattleScene_RebuildScene, which pins it to scene rebuild resource syncing.

name: BattleScene_GetUnitModelSize
summary: Returns the display size used for a battle unit model: id 0x34A uses the global override, otherwise the unit table, then the model record's size word, then a category default (0..4) selected through BattleScene_GetUnitModelVariant.
evidence: The three-tier fallback and the explicit per-variant constants (60.0/80.0/130.0/...) are all visible, and the now-named BattleScene_GetUnitModelVariant supplies the category.

name: Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_SetAnimType
summary: Changes the sprite set's animation type byte +0x37 when the set is active and the value differs, then rebuilds the preset through Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_ApplyPreset so callers can switch between idle/action sprite sets.
evidence: The old/new type comparison and the named Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_ApplyPreset call, together with the handle-validity guard and the callers from the battle menu code, make the setter role explicit.

name: maybe_Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_SetAnimId
signature: void maybe_Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_SetAnimId(SceneSpriteSet* self, unsigned int id, unsigned int arg3, int force)
summary: Selects the sprite set's active id: stores it in f_1E, resolves the 0xD4-stride record and its redirect byte f_D1, then re-applies the preset with the (possibly redirected) id so the new character/animation is built.
evidence: The redirect record layout and the named Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_ApplyPreset call are explicit, and the callers (maybe_Menu_SetSelectedActorId, maybe_Ui_SlotTable_ApplyEntry) select an actor; 'AnimId' is therefore too narrow but the id being a character/animation index is still plausible.

name: maybe_Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_UpdatePresets
summary: Per-frame update of the sprite set's two layers: interpolates the first layer's cloud colours, blends the second layer's presets when the f_35 flag is clear, and, only when the debug global is set, appends the active slot ids to a diagnostic string.
evidence: The main body is the two named preset updaters (Field_Sky_InterpolateCloudColors, Gfx_SceneSpriteSet_BlendPresets); the string building from the old name sits behind the debug flag *0x007A68E0, so 'BuildDebugString' named a side effect instead of the function.

name: Ui_Window_CtorBaseB
summary: Second window base constructor: runs the shared object constructor, installs the plain window vtable 0x78005C and clears the +0x49 state byte; unlike Ui_Window_CtorBase it attaches no layout child.
evidence: Named callees Ui_Object_CtorBase and the callers Ui_BigWindow_CtorBase / Ui_MenuWindow_Ctor / Ui_SkillPanelWindow_Ctor / Ui_ShopWindow_CreateSubObjects show it is the shared window base constructor, not just a vtable store.

name: Field_Scene_IsPointInsideBoxSetC
summary: Tests a world point against the oriented boxes of the scene set at +0x54C: for each typed box it builds the rotation quaternion, transforms the point into box space and returns 1 on the first half-extent hit.
evidence: The point-vs-oriented-box math (quaternion, inverse transform, three half-extent comparisons) is complete and the three named callers (Gfx_SpriteObject_DrawWorldQuad, Field_Marker_DrawOverlay, maybe_Field_CheckCameraOcclusionGate) all need exactly such a test.

name: Camera_UpdateOcclusionAndProjection
summary: Refreshes the camera for this frame: computes the player-state visibility gate, tests whether the camera's view of the player is clear, pushes the player position and the white colour to the camera projection and returns whether both checks passed.
evidence: Named Camera_IsPlayerViewClear, Field_SceneNode_GetPosition and Camera_SetupProjection cover the body, and the returned AND of the state gate with the clear test matches a per-frame camera refresh.

name: maybe_Item_CheckCraftRequirements
signature: u32 maybe_Item_CheckCraftRequirements(u32 arg1, RecipeWork* recipe, u32 scratch, u32 scratch2)
summary: Checks the six 10-byte requirement rows of a recipe: it first bypasses the check when the work's debug/flag bytes are clear, then for each non-empty row compares the item id and the quantity range and stops at the first row whose extra status check fails.
evidence: The row layout (id, min, max, three option bytes) is explicit, but the terminal call is the oddly named maybe_Field_Object_IsStatusFull, so whether this is a craft recipe or another six-entry requirement list cannot be settled.

name: Field_CheckCameraOcclusionGate
summary: Combines three gates into one answer: the player-state allow table, the work's two mode bytes and Camera_IsPlayerViewClear(owner); returns non-zero only when all three pass.
evidence: The AND of the state-table gate, the two work bytes (+0x44/+0x45) and the named Camera_IsPlayerViewClear is explicit, and the sibling 0x00654F90 uses the same gate before pushing the projection.

name: maybe_Field2D_UpdateActorVisuals
summary: Thin wrapper that calls Field2D_ShouldUpdateActorVisual on the field-2D scene object at work+0x88; it ignores its own argument and returns nothing.
evidence: The body is a single call with no use of `actor` and no camera object, so 'UpdateVisibilityForCamera' invented both a per-actor and a camera relationship that the code does not have.

name: maybe_Ui_Part_HasVisibleChild
summary: Returns 1 when any of the object's five sub-parts (+0xE0/+0xE4/+0x110/+0xF8/+0x10C) has its visible byte +0x94 set, and otherwise returns the raw +0x114 field; a null +0xDC pointer or a non-zero vtable+0xC result short-circuits to 1.
evidence: Named callers Battle_TextWindow_UpdateVisibility/Alt and maybe_Field2D_Scene_RenderObjects use it as a 'anything to draw' test, but the final value is the unmodified f_114 field rather than a boolean, so the exact contract is not a pure predicate.

name: maybe_Field2D_Sprite_ChoosePathStep
signature: int maybe_Field2D_Sprite_ChoosePathStep(Field2DSprite* sprite, const short* step, int* bounds)
summary: Chooses the next path step for a field-2D sprite: tests the target box overlap against the sprite position plus the step vector, then picks a random +/- extent from the sprite's 0x2B4 record and clamps it into the bounds. Large parts of the body are unrecoverable.
evidence: The overlap tests and the Math_RandRangeInt(0,2) call are visible, but the body contains halt_baddata and undefined registers (UndefinedInstruction, _SupervisorCall), so even the return value is only partly recoverable.

name: Ui_RecipeBook_FilterNumericRangeAlt
signature: u32 Ui_RecipeBook_FilterNumericRangeAlt(int self, int pool, int mode, u32 clauseValue, int ignoreFlag)
summary: Second recipe-book filter pass: partitions the 64 candidate slots by the entry group returned from vtable+0xD4, applies the numeric clause for modes 1 (count) and 0 (party members) and copies the surviving entries over the pool.
evidence: The caller is the now-named Ui_RecipeBook_ApplyFilterClause, and the mode-specific counts use the named Party_CountActiveInSlot / Ui_Widget_CountChildren before func_00636EE4 evaluates the clause, which pins it to the recipe-book filter.

name: Item_CompareSortKey
signature: bool Item_CompareSortKey(u16 idA, u32 arg2, u16 idB)
summary: Sort comparator for item ids: looks both records up, builds the 32-bit key (record word +0xE, id) and returns true when A's key is smaller; ids without a record use the 0x270F sentinel.
evidence: Its neighbours are the container sort helpers (std_insertion_sort_u16_item, std_introsort_u16_itemB) and the body is a pure 64-bit key comparison, so it is a comparator; +0xE is still an unnamed word, so calling it the 'name' order was an over-claim.

name: Sound_SeqParam_GetWaveRef
signature: unsigned int Sound_SeqParam_GetWaveRef(SoundParamAccessor* self, unsigned int id, unsigned int out2)
summary: Resolves a wave reference for a sequence parameter: takes the base reference from the sequence object, and when the extension object exists and is enabled, merges in its vtable+0x2C result.
evidence: The named base getter maybe_Sound_Seq_GetWaveRefBase plus the enabled-byte guard and the single vtable call show a two-source reference lookup, and all nine callers are sound-bank/voice loaders.

name: Sound_Seq_GetVoiceSlot
signature: unsigned int Sound_Seq_GetVoiceSlot(SoundParamOwner* self, SoundVoiceSlot* out, unsigned int trackIndex, unsigned int rowIndex)
summary: Resolves the voice slot for a (track, row) pair: walks the sequence's track and row tables, bounds-checks the slot index and fills the output descriptor (two table words, a float, a tag pointer and four bytes) from the field accessors.
evidence: The track/row lookup chain, the count bounds check and the now-named maybe_Sound_SeqField_* accessors that fill the descriptor make the voice-slot resolution explicit.

name: maybe_Field2D_Object_NeedsUpdate
summary: Per-object gate used by the Field2D render/update loops: returns 0 only when the object's interface (f_88) reports idle and the payload passes both type checks 0x669B68/0x669B7C, otherwise 1 (process it).
evidence: All six callers are Field2D scene/sprite loops (RenderAll, UpdateSpriteAnimations, Sprite_UpdateLighting, MapChip_QuerySightLine), not UI element code, and the body returns 0 exactly for the fully idle case, so both the 'Ui' subsystem and the 'is interactive' meaning were wrong.

name: maybe_Field2D_Object_NeedsUpdateB
summary: Second copy of the Field2D per-object gate: identical logic to 0x00667AE8 but reading the interface pointer from f_A0 instead of f_88 (the other class's interface slot).
evidence: Same body, same callers and same type checks as 0x00667AE8 with only the interface offset changed, confirming a second Field2D class rather than a UI element test.

name: Container_List_EraseAllNodes
signature: void Container_List_EraseAllNodes(ContainerList* list, ContainerNode* first, ContainerNode* last)
summary: Walks the intrusive node range and erases every node from the owning container through std_RbTree_EraseNode(node, list+4), advancing with the tree successor helpers.
evidence: Every node in the range is passed to the now-named std_RbTree_EraseNode and its callers are the status-window slot release and scene-object destroy paths, so this is a destroy-all walk, not a generic 'apply to each'.

name: maybe_Hid_ReadCalibratedPad
signature: u32* maybe_Hid_ReadCalibratedPad(u32* arg1, u32* b, int count, u32* c, u32* d, u32 e, int f)
summary: Wait/retry wrapper around one IPC read: computes a 3x timeout deadline, sleeps (0x11CC94) and retries while the command reports 0xC8A0CFEF, filling the caller's outputs from Gfx_IpcCmdD0080 when the reply arrives. Large parts of the body are unrecoverable.
evidence: The only named callee is Gfx_IpcCmdD0080 (the shared GPU/IPC event command) and the body still contains halt_baddata plus unaff_r4..r8, so the HID/calibration reading in the old name rests on the caller chain rather than on the recovered code.

name: Gfx_ReadGpuBuffer
signature: int Gfx_ReadGpuBuffer(u32 id, u32 flags, u32 size, u32 offset, u32 arg5, u32 arg6, u32 deadline_lo, u32 deadline_hi)
summary: Reads a GPU buffer through IPC command 0x000C0104 under the scheduler lock: rejects offsets above 0x1000, zeroes the request when either size or offset is empty, releases the session handles when the flag 0x10000 is set and retries on the busy status 0xC8A0CC02 until the deadline.
evidence: The single IPC call is now the named Gfx_IpcCmdC0104, and the surrounding lock/unlock, busy-status retry and deadline arithmetic match the sibling transfer wrapper; the only caller is a graphics path.

name: Gfx_TransferGpuBuffer
signature: int Gfx_TransferGpuBuffer(u32* arg1, u32* b, u8* c, int size, u32* d, int* out, u32 e, u32 f)
summary: Submits a GPU buffer transfer through IPC command 0x000D0080 under the scheduler lock, substituting stack temporaries for null arguments and retrying on the busy status with the 3x timeout; when the caller already holds the current event it forwards to Gfx_WaitGpuEvent instead.
evidence: Named Gfx_IpcCmdD0080, Gfx_WaitGpuEvent and Os_UnlockScheduler cover every step, and the null-argument defaulting pattern is the same as the read wrapper 0x0011A140.

name: Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest
signature: int Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest(u32 cmd, u32 arg2, u32 arg3)
summary: Waits for the service/session to become ready and then sends the caller's request: queries the session info, polls the status command 0x90040 with 10 ms sleeps, runs the setup/close hooks once ready and finally issues the request through Svc_SendRequest3.
evidence: Named callees Svc_QuerySessionInfo and maybe_Svc_SendRequest3 bracket the polling loop, so the function is a 'wait for peer then send' wrapper rather than a generic setup; 'WithSetup' did not say which part was the setup.

name: Gfx_LockedIpcCmd3E0080
summary: Runs the GPU IPC command 0x3E0080 under the global scheduler lock: acquires the lock, takes the service handle, invokes Gfx_IpcCmd3E0080(handle, arg1), asserts on a negative result and unlocks.
evidence: The body neither returns the lock nor leaves it held: it locks, calls the now-named Gfx_IpcCmd3E0080 and unlocks, so 'Os_LockScheduler' named a helper step instead of the actual operation.

name: Svc_WaitForStatusUntilDeadline
signature: u32 Svc_WaitForStatusUntilDeadline(u32 handle, u32 deadline_lo, u32 deadline_hi, u32 flags)
summary: Polls the status command 0x90040 under the scheduler lock and returns 1 as soon as its reply byte is set, or 0 once the 64-bit deadline (with a 3x margin) has passed; sleeps through 0x11CC94 between attempts.
evidence: The body only tests the reply byte of Gfx_IpcCmd90040 against a deadline; it never waits for a tick value itself, so 'WaitUntilTick' named the deadline rather than the operation.

name: Gfx_WriteGpuBuffer
signature: int Gfx_WriteGpuBuffer(u8* arg1, u8* b, u8* c, int size, u8* data, int* out)
summary: Submits a GPU buffer write through IPC command 0x000E0080 under the scheduler lock, replacing null arguments with stack temporaries and returning the service status.
evidence: Named Gfx_IpcCmdE0080 plus the lock/unlock pair and the same null-defaulting pattern as the read/transfer wrappers; the only caller is a graphics path.

name: Os_IpcSendByteLocked
summary: Sends one byte/integer through the IPC helper maybe_Os_IpcSendByte while holding the scheduler lock, and returns its result.
evidence: The body is exactly three statements: lock, maybe_Os_IpcSendByte(arg1), unlock; there is no status decoding, so 'Gfx_QueryStatus' described an interpretation of the result rather than the call.

name: Svc_QuerySessionInfoLocked
signature: void Svc_QuerySessionInfoLocked(u32 kind, u8* outByte, u32* out0, u32* out1, u32* out2)
summary: Queries the session/service info for `kind` under the scheduler lock, asserts on failure and copies the byte plus three words into the caller's optional outputs.
evidence: The single query call is the now-named maybe_Svc_QuerySessionInfo, so the 'thread info' reading was unsupported; the function is a locked query plus output copy.

name: Svc_RequestWithRetry
signature: int Svc_RequestWithRetry(u32 req, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Sends a four-argument service request under the lock and retries while the service answers with one of the three 'try again' codes (0xC8A0CC02 / 0xE0A0CC08 / 0xC8A0CFF0), sleeping 10 time units between attempts and asserting on a hard error.
evidence: Named maybe_Svc_SendRequest4 inside the retry loop and the explicit three-code comparison make the retry contract concrete; the setup hooks around it are shared with Svc_WaitReadyAndSendRequest.

name: maybe_Gfx_ResourceHandle_AcquireType2
summary: Acquires the larger resource type: for an id whose object carries flag 0x20000000 it allocates a 0xE0-byte sprite-animation bank, initialises it with the id, registers it in the owner's handle list and returns the stored handle.
evidence: The ctor is now the named Gfx_SpriteAnimationBank_CreateWithTurns, and the same four callers also use the 0x3C-byte variant 0x001C8704, confirming a resource-type pair; the 'Type2' label still names the variant rather than the concrete resource class.

name: Ui_Overlay_CreateQuadObject
signature: int Ui_Overlay_CreateQuadObject(int parent, int variant, u32* colors)
summary: Creates the full-screen quad used by fade/curtain transitions: sets the 400x240 screen rect and the 12-word colour block on the graphics context, fills the screen-space vertex transform, allocates the 0x224-byte drawable (vtable 0x75A0CC) and registers it.
evidence: The screen rect (0/0/400/240), the 1/aspect scaling and the 0x224 allocation with vtable 0x75A0CC are explicit, and the callers are the fade and poker windows; 'quad object' is what the created drawable is.

name: Ui_ScreenSlideAnim_Update
summary: Three-state per-frame update of a screen slide: state 0 slides the pane offsets at -400 px/s from the current frame delta, state 1 holds for 0.4 s after playing SE 0xD7, and state 2 slides at +400 px/s, clamps to the captured target and copies the target offsets back.
evidence: All constants resolve exactly (400.0/-400.0/0.4), the three states are explicit and the SE/offset-copy steps are visible; the only unnamed callee is the frame-delta getter.

name: Actor_ResetToIdleAction
summary: Resets the actor to idle action 0x1B; when the UI overlay has no active mode it applies the scene node's motion id, and when a mode is active it copies the five display strings from the mode record into the model object and clears the 0x20000000 flag.
evidence: The action id 0x1B and the two branches are explicit, and the string copies now go through the named std_FixedString15_Ctor; the name still covers only the first action, not the display-string refresh.

name: Gfx_Effect_CreateTracked
signature: int Gfx_Effect_CreateTracked(GfxEffectList* self, u32 effectId, u32 effect)
summary: Creates an effect through the effect manager (Mem_AllocHandle on work+0x64), inserts the returned handle into the owner's ordered effect vector (f_760..f_768) and returns its index, or -1 when no effect manager exists.
evidence: The create call on work+0x64 and the insert/count arithmetic are explicit, and the sole caller is the native CreateEffect binding; note the vector-grow branch decompiles into nonsense (f_760 is set to 0), so only the steady-state insert is trustworthy.

name: Gfx_ObjectDesc_InitShared
signature: void Gfx_ObjectDesc_InitShared(ObjectDesc* desc, unsigned int arg2, unsigned int arg3, unsigned int arg4, unsigned int arg5)
summary: Shared object-descriptor initialiser: runs maybe_Gfx_ObjectDesc_Init with the 0x20000000 flag word, installs vtable 0x75EA3C and stores the owner argument at +0x28.
evidence: The named base initialiser and the callers from four UI widget factories plus two battle action constructors show it is the common descriptor setup, not a class-specific one.

name: Ui_GuideWindow_CreateBackgroundSprite
summary: Creates the guide window's background sprite: releases the old handle, builds a 0x220-byte sprite (vtable 0x7737B0) from the fixed descriptor, registers it in the actor list, stores its handle in f_184 and sets the sprite's render modes to 3.
evidence: The described object is a sprite created with the named sprite ctor 0x005F8174 and stored back into the window, and the caller is Ui_GuideWindow_Update; nothing else in the body suggests a different object type.

name: Ui_SkillList_CollectSorted
summary: Rebuilds the 60-entry skill-id list at +0xE: keeps the skills the character may unlock in this slot, sorts them with the shared quicksort plus the inlined insertion sort by id byte, writes the count and pads the rest with 0xFFFF.
evidence: Named SkillPanel_CanUnlockSkill decides membership and std_quicksort_4byte_bytekey is the sort core, so 'collect and sort the skill list' is exactly what the body does; the 60-entry layout matches the skill helpers.

name: Ui_ScreenSlideAnim_Start
summary: Starts a screen slide: clears the UI slide flag, opens the 2D effect pass, caches the owner and every child pane's +0x9C offset, snapshots the 57 layout records (12 fields each) into the animation state, plays SE 0xD4 and resets the state byte.
evidence: The 57-record snapshot loop, the SE 0xD4 play and the state reset to 0 match the update function at 0x004F08F8, which consumes exactly these fields.

name: maybe_Field2D_MapChip_UpdateRegion
signature: void maybe_Field2D_MapChip_UpdateRegion(Field2DMap* self, int arg2, int arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Chooses and runs the region pass for a Field2D map: dispatches on the chip mode byte to Field2D_MapChip_ScanRegionTiles, BuildCollisionMask or QueryCollision, and for the random mode first counts the chips per layer, picks one at random and then builds the mask.
evidence: The three named region builders are called as alternatives, so this is a dispatcher over the region passes rather than a 'collect into a list'; the meaning of the per-layer counter array is still unclear.

name: maybe_Field_FindOverlapIndex
signature: int maybe_Field_FindOverlapIndex(u32 arg1, u32 shapeHandle, int* idsA, int idCountA, int* idsB, int idCountB, u32 mask, int start)
summary: Walks idsA from `start`, skips the ids also present in idsB, resolves the remaining object and, when its flag word matches `mask` and its condition/group reference is active, applies the attribute hook for shapeHandle; returns start+1 on the first hit.
evidence: Named maybe_Field_Condition_HasActiveRef, maybe_Field_Object_HasActiveGroupRef, maybe_Gfx_ModelPart_ApplyAttribute and maybe_Field_Object_UpdateHook show the per-candidate test, but the returned value is an index advance, so the 'overlap' wording is only the old interpretation.

name: Ui_Part_SelectChildParts
signature: int Ui_Part_SelectChildParts(Ui_Part* part, const Ui_PartOwner* owner, const u8* kindRecord)
summary: Selects and creates the child parts for a UI part kind: snapshots the kind table, creates the primary child, collects the owner's entries whose type byte matches, picks one at random and creates the three child parts at +0x00/+0x10/+0x20.
evidence: Named maybe_Ui_Part_CreateChildPart/CreateChildPartEx cover every creation step, and the owner-entry filter on the kind record's byte +1 is explicit; the random pick is the 'select' part of the name.

name: maybe_FieldParty_UpdateMemberFade
summary: Advances the party group's fade offsets: compares the group's f_1C and every member float at +0x20.. with the frame delta and adds -400.0 * dt to each once the delta has passed, then plays the idle animation when the members are done.
evidence: The same -400.0 constant and offset-array pattern as the screen slide, plus the named Actor_PlayIdleAnimationForState call, support a fade/slide helper; the meaning of the per-member float array is still inferred.

name: maybe_Field2D_MapChip_GetFlags
signature: u32 maybe_Field2D_MapChip_GetFlags(u32 arg1, u32 chipId, u32 arg3, u32 vm)
summary: Resolves a map chip record and, when it carries flag 1 plus 0x20000000/0x20000, returns whether the condition reference at +0x3C is active; otherwise returns 0.
evidence: The body ends in maybe_Field_Condition_HasActiveRef on chip+0x3C and returns its result, so it queries an attached condition rather than reading a chip flag word.

name: maybe_Battle_IsUnitSoundFinished
summary: Returns 1 only when every unit in the four battle unit lists has finished its sound: per unit it checks the widget state (8), the 0x20000000 flag and the remaining playback time, returning 0 as soon as one is still running.
evidence: The lists walked are the battle work's four unit lists at +0x4298 (established layout), the entry id is f_1DA, and the 0 return happens exactly when a sound has time left, so the 'Ui widget sound busy' reading named the wrong subsystem.

name: Ui_Part_CollectSlots
summary: Collects the part's four non-null child slots at +0xC0..+0xCC into a temporary vector, sorts them by their +0x26C value, and writes the resulting draw order (descending index) into each slot's +0x295 byte.
evidence: The named maybe_Ui_SortSlotsByValue call plus the explicit +0x295 draw-order stores make the collection/draw-order role concrete; the remaining callees are the 2D layout/order helpers.

name: Container_RemoveValueFromVector
summary: Erases every occurrence of `value` from the integer vector at f_BC->f_5C..f_9C using the std::remove compaction, updates the element count at f_9C and returns the new end pointer (or 0 when there is no vector).
evidence: The body is exactly the inlined std::remove loop plus the count store, and the helper 0x004C3944 supplies begin/end; nothing else is touched.

name: Container_SortedInsertU16
summary: Inserts a 16-bit id (taken from the record's word +4) into the descending fixed list at +8 by binary search plus tail shift, ignores duplicates and bumps the count at +0x1054; the companion word at +2 comes from the record's second table.
evidence: The binary search over 4-byte entries, the duplicate check and the count increment are all explicit, and the caller is the quest/flag list collector.

name: Actor_Action_Trail_Update
summary: Per-frame update of the after-image action: advances the action clock and every trail timestamp by dt*scale, clamps them to the newest sample f_48 and, once all samples have caught up, marks the action finished (f_68 = 1) and plays the idle animation.
evidence: The dt*scale advance, the clamp to f_48, the completion flag store and the named Actor_PlayIdleAnimationForState call are all visible in one short function.

name: Sound_DspChannel_Flush
summary: Sets the 0x20000000 command bit in one DSP channel's command word under the sound monitor and returns 1, or 0 when the sound system is not initialised.
evidence: The body is a single read-modify-write of the channel word selected by the driver's active-bank bit, wrapped in the sound monitor; the only uncertainty is what the 0x20000000 bit means (flush/key-off), which the callers after a key-on support.

name: maybe_Field2D_MapChip_FilterObjectsByFlag
signature: int* maybe_Field2D_MapChip_FilterObjectsByFlag(int* begin, int* end, u32 flag, int* out, int arg5, int arg6)
summary: Walks a list of object ids and, for each chip carrying the 0x40 flag and an active condition reference, runs one of four movement queries (arg6 selects the direction/edge) and returns the current iterator on a hit.
evidence: The body never writes into `out`; it returns the iterator when maybe_Field_Condition_HasActiveRef plus one of the edge/move queries succeeds, so 'filter objects by flag' described only the guard, not the search.

name: maybe_Field2D_MapChip_FindReachableCell
signature: u32* maybe_Field2D_MapChip_FindReachableCell(u32* out, u32 map, u32 startCell, int* list, int count, char dir)
summary: Searches the candidate chip list for the first chip that allows a move in direction `dir`: checks the chip's 0x400/0x800 flag, its active condition reference and the move query, returning the list iterator on a hit.
evidence: The two direction flags (0x400 horizontal / 0x800 vertical), the condition check and the shared move query make the search readable; what the result is used for (path step vs. reachability test) is still open.

name: maybe_Field2D_Map_SelectLayerRange
signature: void maybe_Field2D_Map_SelectLayerRange(int self, unsigned int arg2, unsigned int layerTag, unsigned int* first, unsigned int* last)
summary: Rebuilds the map's active object for a layer: releases the old object at +0x2FE0, copies the requested entry range into a stack buffer and builds a new object through Field2D_MapChip_QuerySightLine with the map root and the layer tag.
evidence: The release/rebuild sequence and the named Field2D_MapChip_QuerySightLine call are visible, but the range copy decompiles into a broken 3-word buffer (the local array is smaller than the copied range), so the exact range contract is unreliable.

name: Os_IsSessionRunnable
summary: Returns 1 only when the service session is open and its status word has both the connected (0x20000000) and ready (0x10000000) bits set.
evidence: The open-flag query and the two status bits are the whole body, and its only caller 0x0010D430 uses the result to decide whether to arm the in-call flag.

name: Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_UpdateLinkState
summary: Slot 14 of the member-widget class: when the linked actor has flag bit 0x20000000 or 0x40000000 set it runs the matching vtable pair, calls the link/unlink pass (maybe_Battle_Ui_LinkMemberActors or its B twin) and clears that bit.
evidence: The two named link passes, the two bit masks and the matching clears are all explicit, and the unnamed vtable slots around them are the per-state setup calls.

name: Snd_SetChannelLength
signature: unsigned int Snd_SetChannelLength(ChannelBuffer* buf, unsigned int length)
summary: Writes a channel's loop length: clamps the value to 0x7FFF, stores it as a halfword in the channel block and sets the 0x20000000 update bit.
evidence: The clamp, the halfword store and the dirty-bit set are explicit; which channel register the field is remains inferred from the 24-channel bank layout shared with the other setters.

name: Gfx_Sprite_InitParams
signature: GfxSprite* Gfx_Sprite_InitParams(GfxSpriteManager* mgr, ResDesc* desc, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Allocates a sprite/effect slot through the manager and installs the default parameter block: vtable 0x7642D4, zero origin, alpha 0xFF, two 0xFFFF limits and the -1/-8 sentinels.
evidence: The named sprite-slot allocator (0x005F8174) and the fixed default block make this an initialiser; the argument-derived word at desc+4 is the only caller-supplied value.

name: Gfx_Sprite_InitParamsAlt
summary: Second sprite initialiser: allocates the slot, installs vtable 0x76438C and writes the alternate default block (zero origin then 1.5 scale, 0xFFFF/0xFF limits and the +0x221 flag byte set to 1).
evidence: Same allocation call as 0x0032DB00 but a different vtable and default block, so this is the second variant of the same sprite constructor.

name: Field_SceneObject_CtorWithDefaults
signature: void* Field_SceneObject_CtorWithDefaults(u32 owner, int* params, u32 flags)
summary: Constructs a scene object with the default part/colour data: allocates through the sprite-slot allocator with flag 0x20000000, installs vtable 0x765340, copies the two eight-word default tables, and fills the id/flag/scale fields and the empty handle sentinels.
evidence: The allocation call, the two identical default-table copies and the explicit sentinel stores (0xFFFFF800, -1, 0xFF) match the sibling Field_SceneObjectSprite_Ctor family.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_DeletingDtor
summary: Deleting destructor of the message window: destroys the message page at +0x1E18, restores the remaining sub-object vtables, destroys the two 0x414-byte containers and the list node, releases the layout references and frees the window.
evidence: The named Ui_MessagePage_Dtor/Ui_LayoutRef_Release/Ui_Object_DtorBase calls and the final operator delete make this the deleting destructor, but the name Ui_MessageWindow_Dtor is already taken by the earlier 0x001C57E4 window, so the deleting variant gets the distinct name.

name: Ui_MessageWindow_Dtor_Large
summary: Deleting destructor of the largest message-window variant: tears down the extra members in reverse order (the 0x18-entry array at -0x28CC, the model block, the list nodes and the message page) and re-splices each intrusive list before releasing the final sub-object.
evidence: Same teardown sequence and literal-pool addresses as 0x002E4D08 plus the additional std_destroy_range/array and list re-splice pairs; the name keeps it distinguishable from the smaller variant.

name: Battle_TextWindow_CtorPane
summary: In-place constructor of the battle text window's pane object: runs the window base constructor, installs vtable 0x761474, initialises the member pair at +0x48 with its back-pointer and default-constructs the five 0x18-byte child state objects.
evidence: The body is a constructor chain (base ctor, vtable store, Ui_Object_InitMemberPair, std_ConstructArray of 5 children) and the only caller is Battle_TextWindow_Ctor, so 'InitTextPane' understated that it creates the object.
